description: Announced Aug. 5 at Cornell Tech, a research partnership will help neighborhoods in Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx identify where new trees are needed most to improve public health.

title: Redesigned fire gear offers potentially more cooling, less toxicity
description: A Cornell researcher’s bold redesign of firefighter gear, which hasn’t significantly changed in decades, is more versatile and better adapted to their actual work, only a small fraction of which involves fighting structure fires.

title: Near Liberty Bell, public art lets freedom ring for US at 250
description: Part of Philadelphia's semiquincentennial celebrations, an interactive bell tower designed by Paul Ramírez Jonas invites visitors to reflect on the meaning of freedom.

title: AAP students lend their creativity to a new vision for 4-H camp
description: After Camp Owahta’s arts and crafts building burned down last summer, the Cortland County camp’s leadership turned to second-year architecture students for fresh ideas.

title: Cornell Tech announces the 2026 Startup Awards and the Inaugural Frontiers of AI Summit
description: As the 2025–26 academic year comes to a close, Cornell Tech will host a series of events throughout May showcasing student achievement, entrepreneurship, design, and the future of emerging technologies.

title: Building and Unbuilding the City Museum: From Le Corbusier to Ahmedabad
description: Architecture Associate Professor Lily Chi in collaboration with architect and educator Sarosh Anklesaria (M.Arch. II ’08) coedited this collection of essays examining the cultural center’s ambitious beginning, present precarity, and possible futures.

title: Philosophy and art faculty win Guggenheim fellowships
description: Kate A. Manne, professor of philosophy, and Leeza Meksin, assistant professor of art, have been named 2026 fellows by the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation.

title: Annabelle Selldorf: The courage to make noise
description: This spring’s L. Michael Goldsmith Lecture will feature guest speaker Annabelle Selldorf, founding principal of Selldorf Architects.

title: Memory becomes muse in annual runway show
description: The 42nd annual Cornell Fashion Collective Spring Runway Show paid homage to well-loved storybooks and designers’ childhood memories and cultural backgrounds.

title: Announcing: Cornell Journal of Architecture Issue 13, “Missing”
description: Concluding a thematic set spanning three issues and marking the 45th anniversary of its inaugural volume, this student-led publication continues to capture current thinking in the field and reinforce the importance of writing and editing in an architectural education. A launch event is scheduled for April 10.

title: Materials, machines, mentorship shape student spring runway show
description: The annual Cornell Fashion Collective Spring Runway Show, on March 21, will feature the work of fashion design majors as well as students from across the university who are looking to broaden their Cornell experience.

title: Enter the dragon: Milestone Dragon Day to take viewers inside
description: Celebrating a tradition born 125 years ago, first-year architecture students on March 27 will parade a dragon they've designed through campus, then invite community members to tour its interior.

title: Renowned artist Jeffrey Gibson to give public talk March 24
description: Artist Jeffrey Gibson, whose immersive work explores ideas around belonging, will give a public talk March 24 as the spring 2026 Cooper Visiting Artist Lecture Series speaker at the College of Architecture, Art and Planning.

title: RBG’s influences featured in ‘Fashioning Justice’ exhibit
description: Ruth Bader Ginsburg ’54 was a champion for women’s equality. Her style, and the substance behind it, will be on display in an exhibit, “Fashioning Justice: Ruth Bader Ginsburg ’54 and the Power of Presence.”

title: Cornell faculty and staff honored for community-engaged innovation
description: Fourteen members of Cornell’s faculty and staff are being recognized this year with Community-Engaged Practice and Innovation Awards from the David M. Einhorn Center for Community Engagement.

title: EdemaFlex: soft-robotic glove for swelling relief
description: EdemaFlex, a new glove with more than three dozen actuators across all five fingers and the palm, developed by Cornell researchers, aims to reduce swelling for people suffering from edema.

title: Local volunteer powers rural resilience with student support
description: Cornell will honor longtime volunteer Beth Harrington on Feb. 5 for her work to make the Town of Caroline more resilient in the face of emergencies, with support from a team of graduate students.

title: Underwater 3D printing could transform maritime construction
description: An interdisciplinary collaboration has developed a way to 3D-print concrete underwater – a technique that could transform on-site maritime construction and the repair of critical infrastructure.

title: Designing the future: a Q&A with Harald Haraldsson
description: Through rapid prototyping and creative experimentation, Harald and his students explore how emerging technologies can reshape the way we interact with both digital and physical environments.

title: What's ahead: Cornell AAP spring 2026 highlights
description: After a winter break to regroup and recharge, faculty, students, and staff return to campus and to the open questions, conversations, and explorations that will drive the work of the semester ahead.

title: Artist team Mendi + Keith Obadike named USA Fellows
description: The Obadikes have exhibited and performed their interdisciplinary work at The New Museum, The Studio Museum in Harlem, The Whitney Museum of American Art, New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art, and The Museum of Modern Art. Their projects include four books, two albums, and a series of large-scale public sound artworks.

title: Imagining and building post-crisis places
description: AAP professor Esra Akcan’s new book examines architecture’s role as both a cause of human casualties and an agent for the public good with the potential to ameliorate traumas following conflict and crises.

title: 2025 Year in Review
description: Cornell’s impact was felt near and far, from the lacrosse fields to research labs and beyond in a turbulent 2025.

title: From Milstein scholar to design tech pioneer
description: Julia Beitel is pursuing a master’s in Design Technology at Cornell Tech, creating projects that fuse design, sustainability, and technology.

title: Seamless tech: ‘OriStitch’ threads computation and 3D textiles
description: Researchers from the Cornell Bowers have developed OriStitch, a new software and fabrication system that takes simple 3D objects and spins them into a design for a textile version using carefully placed stitches in fabric.

title: Bird-of-paradise inspires darkest fabric ever made
description: The color “ultrablack” has a variety of uses, including in cameras, solar panels and telescopes, but it’s difficult to produce and can appear less black when viewed at an angle. A Cornell lab has devised a simple method for making the elusive color.

title: Gala inspires students to find their fit in fashion industry
description: A festive black-tie gala brought together fashion industry star power, networking opportunities and Cornell fashion students wearing shimmering gowns and fashion-forward tuxedos.

title: Bone density builder wins top prize at food hackathon
description: The weekend event involved more than 150 undergraduate and graduate students from across Cornell.

title: At COP30, floating plaza shifts perspective of sea-level rise
description: At United Nations climate meetings in Brazil, a floating pavilion whose designers include AAP's J. Meejin Yoon offers delegates a "surreal" eye-level view of the water.

title: ‘Fit for Duty’ explores military uniforms’ influence on fashion
description: Opening on Veterans Day, the Cornell Fashion + Textile Collection exhibition traces the interplay of form and function across conflict and couture – while highlighting Cornell’s land-grant legacy of military service.

title: Certification promotes being ‘age friendly’ as good business
description: Assisted by Cornell faculty and students, Tompkins County has launched a program to recognize businesses for efforts to welcome patrons across the age spectrum.

title: Cornell AAP to launch first New York City-based high school summer program
description: The College of Architecture, Art, and Planning is adding a new summer intensive for high schoolers interested in studying the collective aspirations, methodologies, and processes involved in the design of cities.

title: Sacramento International Airport commissions Art Chair Paul Ramírez Jonas to create permanent public installation
description: Using imagery and words that celebrate the surrounding valley as well as airport staff, Ramírez Jonas has revealed preliminary models of the full work, which will wrap the transportation hub's new six-story parking facility.

title: Gensler Family AAP NYC Center opens doors, possibilities on Cornell Tech Campus
description: After a decade at 26 Broadway in Lower Manhattan, the center's move to Roosevelt Island affords new opportunities for connection and collaboration.

title: Reusable nanofiber membrane filters water sustainably
description: A Cornell research group has developed a cyclodextrin-based fibrous membrane that in lab testing removed approximately 90% of aqueous triclosan, an antibacterial agent that poses a threat to aquatic organisms.

title: Cornell Tech hosts first-ever summit on disability, access, and AI
description: The summit brought together researchers, technologists, and community advocates to explore how disability and accessibility intersect with innovation.

title: Built on curiosity: architecture and the public realm
description: Rubacha Featured Speakers Susan Rodriguez ('81, B.Arch. '82) and Michael Manfredi (M.Arch. '80) will deliver lectures on Thursday, October 23, at 5:30 p.m. in the Abby and Howard Milstein Auditorium on Cornell's Ithaca campus. In advance of their talks, Rodriguez and Manfredi share insights drawn from their professional trajectories.

title: Generative art enhances virtual shopping experience
description: Art infusion theory – the idea that displaying art in retail settings can positively impact consumer behavior – can be applied to the metaverse with similar results, a Cornell design researcher has shown.

title: Midwest art installation pushes boundaries of urban space
description: For Exhibit Columbus - a prominent stage for emerging designers - Michael Jefferson and Suzanne Lettieri used chromakeyed colors to create an "urban cinema screen" at a downtown plaza.

title: Teens’ portraits celebrate Toni Morrison as community-builder
description: High schoolers from Ithaca and Brooklyn produced the artworks depicting Morrison and a local student, a collaboration that promises to introduce Morrison's work to new generations of New Yorkers.

title: The secret history of NYC’s most iconic landscapes
description: In his new book, Cornell professor and historian Thomas J. Campanella shines a light on a pair of alumni from a century ago who helped create some of New York City’s most recognizable sights but have been largely overlooked.

title: Faculty awarded entrepreneurship funding
description: The Louis H. Zalaznick Teaching Assistantships help faculty develop or expand courses, pursue research opportunities or add teaching assistants.

title: Entrepreneurial students flock to kickoff event
description: The event featured more than 30 resource tables and pitches from four students hoping to be part of eLab.

title: Rooms with a ‘view score’: Software aids building designers
description: Viewscore.io can simulate and score occupants' satisfaction with window views, helping designers optimize buildings' facades, floor plans and energy efficiency.

title: En route to Brazil, AquaPraça floats new responses to rising seas in Venice
description: An international coalition of architects, including AAP Dean J. Meejin Yoon and alumnus Eric Höweler, governmental agencies, NGOs, and other partners unveiled AquaPraça, a submersible public plaza designed to advance civic discourse on climate change, at La Biennale di Venezia before the project departs for COP30 in Brazil.

title: New faculty José Sánchez wants you to play with architecture — literally
description: José Sánchez doesn’t just design buildings. He designs games that teach people how to build a better world.

title: Cornell Tech’s new faculty are building tech that thinks, feels, and teaches
description: With three Sloan Fellows, three NSF CAREER Award winners, and a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree among them, this year’s new faculty cohort arrives with notable accolades and ambitions.

title: Pursuing purpose, building knowledge: AAP embarks on the fall 2025 semester
description: Aligned with an ongoing mission to advance research, scholarship, and creative practices, Cornell's College of Architecture, Art, and Planning begins a vibrant semester of critical and creative work that invites students, faculty, and staff to explore ideas across disciplines in pursuit of a more sustainable and equitable world.

title: ‘Ultra-fresh’ fashion reshapes the industry, with a cost to the environment
description: New research from Cornell SC Johnson College of Business explores how Asian companies are producing ultra-fresh fashion with rapid product launches, digital supply chains and customer engagement strategies – but also presents sustainability challenges.

title: Building energy model offers cities decarbonization roadmap
description: Using Ithaca as a case study, researchers have demonstrated a software tool that can quickly model building energy use and simulate the most cost-effective strategies for improving efficiency and reducing emissions.

title: Moaning for the Mainland: How Taiwan Satisfies China's Lust for Pornography
description: Pornographic material is strictly forbidden in the People's Republic of China. Yet demand is high nonetheless. Many of the films are produced in Taiwan – but performers do their best to conceal that fact.

title: The New Axis of Evil: DER SPIEGEL Investigation Reveals Deep Military Cooperation between Russia and China
description: Reporting by DER SPIEGEL and its partners provide a detailed and unprecedented look at the depth of military cooperation between Russia and China. Secret documents show the plans the two countries are developing.

title: New Information in the Nazi Database: What You Need to Know About the SS
description: Your grandfather appears in the SS files? What that might mean, how you can continue your research and who was even allowed to join the Nazi organization in the first place: You'll find answers to the most important questions here.

title: 250 Years: American Democracy Has Survived 250 Years, But Can It Survive Trump?
description: Democracy is a tenacious beast, but it has been riven by contradictions ever since the Declaration of Independence. Nowhere are those contradictions in such sharp relief as in Trump's America.

title: In Trump's Colony: Does the US Really Hold the Reins in Venezuela?
description: Shortly before the earthquakes, DER SPIEGEL traveled to Venezuela to explore the question: Who is really in charge in the country?

title: The Minab Attack: Did the United States Commit a War Crime in Iran?
description: The Feb. 28 attack on an elementary school in Minab, Iran, likely killed dozens of children and evidence suggests the US may be responsible. But was it a war crime? DER SPIEGEL took a closer look.

title: Climate Change in Oceania: Tuvalu Is Tired of the Prophets of Doom
description: As ocean waters continue to rise, the Pacific island nation of Tuvalu became a symbol of climate change. Residents, though, are fed up with being seen by the world as the canaries in the coalmine.

title: The Mystery of Michele: A Missing Woman from Germany Reappears in the Epstein Files
description: A young woman from Germany vanished without a trace 11 years ago. Now, her name makes several appearances in the Epstein files. Her family wants to finally learn what happened to her.

title: Our Warming Climate: A Pilot Project in Norway Raises Doubts about CCS Sustainability
description: Can Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) really improve the climate balance of cement production? Shortcomings in Norway have some wondering if it has a future in industrial settings.

title: Hungarian Premier Péter Magyar: 'Our Country Was a Hostage State'
description: After 16 years of Viktor Orbán's rule, it looked to many as though democracy in Hungary was dead. But not to Péter Magyar. DER SPIEGEL spoke with him about how he managed to boot out the autocrat.

title: NSDAP archive: How DER SPIEGEL processed the data from the Nazi card file
description: Where does the data come from? What do the matches mean? What errors exist? And what does the date of joining reveal about entanglement with Hitler’s regime? Here you can find the answers to the most important questions about the Nazi card file.

title: Interactive Research Tool: What Your Family Did Under Hitler – Find Out Here
description: DER SPIEGEL has cross-referenced hundreds of thousands of SS files with the millions of NSDAP membership cards. Here, you can search through the updated files and find clues as to possible SS membership.

title: Human Rights in the US: Meet the Transgender Americans Forced to Flee GOP Persecution
description: Cerberus has their go-bag ready. Adrian is prepared to move at a moment's notice. Debra Guckenheimer has already fled the US with her nonbinary children. The GOP transgender assault is driving people from their homes - and their country.

title: An Interview with Maduro's Son: "We Should Have Done More to Protect My Father"
description: Nicolás Maduro Guerra, son of the imprisoned Venezuelan strongman, speaks to a Western media outlet for the first time about his father's mistakes and his own underestimation of US power.

title: Forced Mercenaries: How Russia Dupes Kenyans into Fighting in Ukraine
description: One thought he was getting a job driving a truck in Russia. Another says he was invited to run in a race. Both ended up being forced to fight in Putin's war.

title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: "I Am Dissatisfied with the Prevailing Atmosphere in Germany"
description: In a wide ranging interview with DER SPIEGEL, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz speaks about his relationship with Trump, the immense challenges facing Germany and the dangers of the AfD.

title: Ten Years after the End of the One-Child Policy: A Visit to Ground Zero of China's Aging Population
description: Ten years ago, China brought the one-child policy to an end. In Rudong, the city where the policy was originally tested, 40 percent of residents are over the age of 60 - a preview of what is to come.

title: Terror Records in German Hands: ISIS and the Bureaucracy of Evil
description: DER SPIEGEL has learned that German authorities have obtained detailed membership lists kept by the terror group Islamic State. Some suspected terrorists are apparently still living in Germany.

title: The War in Ukraine: As Russian Losses Mount, Signing Bonuses for Recruits Are Skyrocketing
description: It is becoming increasingly difficult for Russian officials to meet the recruitment quotas set by Moscow. In response, bonuses are rising and standards are plummeting, as DER SPIEGEL has learned.

title: Defense in Orbit: Germany Goes Big in the Military Space Race
description: Berlin was long content to ignore space as a military frontier. But now, the Merz government is investing 35 billion euros in an array of new systems. The race for lucrative contracts has begun.

title: Jason Arday: Ex-Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism scandal found dead
description: Jason Arday, the youngest ever Black professor at Cambridge, was found unresponsive at an address in London. Arday had recently resigned in the midst of a plagiarism row.

title: Vast German wildfire forces evacuation in Eifel forest
description: Firefighters tackling the biggest forest fire in the history of North-Rhine Westfalia say residents are unlikely to be able to return on Friday amid high temperatures, humidity and wind. DW has the latest.

title: In Germany record heat meets climate action fatigue
description: For the German government climate action does not seem to be a priority — despite record temperatures, heat-related deaths and drought. Why don't more people take to the streets in protest?

title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges in Brian Thompson death
description: The plea resolves the remaining federal charges tied to the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson and could affect a separate New York state case.

title: Germany news: Car industry hemorrhaging jobs
description: The country's famed auto sector is losing jobs faster than any industrial branch in the economy, official statistics show. Meanwhile, farmers say drought conditions could affect this year's harvest. DW has more.

title: France: Top watchdog blocks social media ban for children
description: Denying access to platforms such as Facebook, TikTok and YouTube for under-15s would infringe upon freedom of expression, the Constitutional Council has said.

title: Eco wins: A Dutch lab for crops, a climate-ready city, and a beaver comeback
description: Dutch crops hit the "climate gym," a German city is preparing for more extreme weather, and beavers are restoring rivers across Europe. This week's eco wins are all about building and adapting to a changing climate.

title: Taliban pressured by insurgents after 5 years in power
description: The Taliban managed to retake power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021. Now, they face armed factions who challenge the Taliban rule and strain their central claim of providing security.

title: Congo: Ebola cases are rising at record pace
description: The Ebola virus is spreading rapidly in the DRC. In Kinshasa, a city of millions, fears of a serious health crisis are growing. Hospitals are scrambling to prepare for emergencies as best as they can.

title: Fact check: False claims target US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
description: Abdul El-Sayed, who could become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he wins in November, has been targeted by false claims online following his victory in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary.

title: Can a giant Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
description: Europe's largest statue of the Virgin Mary will be inaugurated on Saturday in the Polish village of Konotopie. What will the monument mean for the village it towers over and for the Catholic faith in Poland in general?

title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Latvia
description: Jets have shot down a foreign drone over Latvia after it entered the Baltic state's airspace. Its origin remains unclear, but the incident adds to concern over repeated incursions along NATO's eastern flank.

title: Zambia vote count resumes after suspension amid reports of violence
description: Earlier, the electoral commission suspended vote counting after alleged attacks on polling staff and the theft of marked ballot papers.

title: Berlin's Russian House: A hub for propaganda and espionage?
description: The Russian House stands in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it's being used to spread propaganda for Putin's Russia. Now, French authorities have said it is being used by the Kremlin for espionage.

title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
description: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.

title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
description: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

title: UK: Nigel Farage beats a trash can in Clacton by-election
description: Nigel Farage reclaimed his Clacton seat with 63% of the vote, but his main rival, Count Binface, took over a quarter, as Farage skipped the count citing security concerns.

title: India news: 7 dead, 3 trapped in Uttarakhand tunnel collapse
description: A rescue operation is continuing after a tunnel disaster in India's Uttrakhand state. And the results of a probe into an Air India flight that suffered a 300-foot drop are out. DW has more.

title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
description: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.

title: Four dead, thousands stranded as record rain lashes Japan
description: Unprecedented rainfall in Japan's Chiba prefecture has stranded thousands of passengers at Tokyo's Narita airport and prompted authorities to issue the highest-level rain warning for the first time.

title: Romania shuts nuclear plant, Hungary dams dry Danube River
description: Romania has shut down its only nuclear plant in a rare move prompted by the lack of cooling water from the Danube River. Hungary, meanwhile, is racing to dam the Danube, trying to keep its Paks plant online.

title: Ukraine's monthly civilian casualties highest since 2022
description: UN monitors say civilian casualties in Ukraine hit their highest monthly level since the start of Russia's full-scale war. The latest attacks included a Russian drone strike on a train, killing two workers.

title: How Germany's drone defense fails
description: Drone defense is a priority for the German government. The latest dramatic incident involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport shows there are still substantial shortcomings.

title: Germany news: Far-right leader backs left-wing populist
description: The leader of the far-right AfD in Thuringia, Björn Höcke, has offered to back populist Sahra Wagenknecht as state premier. And heat-related deaths this year are now numbered at some 12,500. DW has more.

title: Does the clean energy transition need forever chemicals?
description: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
description: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

title: Why is Russia's Yabloko party barred from upcoming election?
description: Russia's highest court has banned anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary election. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in the country?

title: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
description: A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.

title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
description: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

title: Unconstitutional? German intelligence to receive more powers
description: German intelligence agencies have been calling for more powers in the fight against cyberattacks, terrorism and extremism. Now the government has given the go. Critics warn that red lines are being crossed.

title: Italy: Etna eruption in Sicily halts Catania flights
description: Sicily's Catania airport has suspended flights again as Mount Etna continues to spew lava and volcanic ash. The eruption has disrupted travel during the peak summer holiday season.

title: Short on US Patriot missiles, Ukraine looks for alternatives
description: Russia is putting pressure on Ukraine with ballistic missiles, but Kyiv is short of Patriot interceptors. Domestic production and European alternatives take time. Can Kyiv realistically reduce its dependence on the US?

title: Germany news: Cabinet approves intelligence service reforms
description: Germany's domestic and foreign intelligence services are to get greater powers to deal with hybrid threats. Meanwhile, transport ministers are meeting to find solutions to increasingly low river levels.

title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
description: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
description: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.

title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
description: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

title: Can Turkey's new PKK law bring peace?
description: Turkey's parliament has passed a framework law for the peace process with the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK). What does it stipulate, why is it controversial and what does it mean for the future of the peace process?

title: Hungary's parliament elects Orban critic as new president
description: Hungary's parliament has overwhelmingly confirmed Andras Baka, formerly the head of the Supreme Court, to the largely ceremonial role of president. New Prime Minister Peter Magyar controversially removed his predecessor.

title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
description: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

title: Afghanistan, the Taliban and German promises
description: After the Taliban retook power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021, Berlin promised to bring all the Afghan local staff members to Germany. But people are still waiting to leave in Pakistan and Afghanistan.

title: Bulgaria drone crash a wake-up call for country's defenses
description: The explosion of a Ukrainian decoy drone in Bulgaria near the Romanian border reveals gaps in Bulgaria's defenses, raises questions and shines a light on the country's policy shift on the war in Ukraine.

title: Germany news: Some shipping stops as Rhine hits new lows
description: The summer heat is not only causing water levels in Germany's key river arteries to drop to dangerously low levels, but also contributing to wildfires in several areas. Follow DW for more.

title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
description: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

title: Turkey MPs back historic law on reintegrating PKK militants
description: Turkey's parliament has taken a major step toward ending four decades of conflict with the PKK. The new law sets out how some militants can return to civilian life, but leaves Abdullah Ocalan's future unresolved.

title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
description: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
description: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.

title: When extreme heat threatens Europe's nuclear power
description: Warm rivers and low water levels are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output across Europe. Over a year, the losses are minimal, but on critical days the loss of power has consequences for grids and prices.

title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
description: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.

title: Western Europe records hottest June and July on record
description: Drought is gripping large parts of Europe, with soils unusually dry and major rivers running low. A strengthening El Nino could push global temperatures even higher later this year.

title: Germany news: Berlin to step up drone security research
description: Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said Germany is moving to counter the threats posed by drones. Meanwhile, the transport minister said he wants Deutsche Bahn bonuses tied to punctuality targets.

title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
description: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.

title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
description: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

title: Germany: Interior Minister warns of 'daily' hybrid warfare
description: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says attacks by foreign powers have become a constant threat to Germany. His remarks come just days after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig airport.

title: Kosovo PM Kurti egged in parliament amid political crisis
description: Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.

title: When German Catholics and Protestants share a church
description: Each year, dozens of churches are decommissioned, demolished or repurposed in Germany. But there is a new, unique development.

title: Germany debates reintroducing mandatory civilian service
description: Social organizations are skeptical about the government's ideas for a civilian service program that youths could choose as an alternative should Germany reinstate mandatory military conscription.

title: Ceuta: Spain sets up border controls on travelers from Italy
description: Spain had warned Italy it would impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.

title: Iceland's EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
description: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.

title: Migrant tunnels in Lithuania direct suspicion towards Minsk
description: Lithuania's border guards have discovered tunnels through which migrants are trying to enter the country from Belarus. Analysts see them as a means to destabilize the country.

title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy makes first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia
description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia. His host, President Aleksandar Vucic, hopes to score points with the EU, while Zelenskyy seeks more arms from a country that remains friendly to Russia.

title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
description: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

title: Germany: Far-right AfD extends its lead in nationwide polls
description: In the latest Sunday poll, the AfD continues to pull ahead. And more and more people are against excluding the right-wing populists from decision-making, at least on a case-by-case basis.

title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
description: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
description: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
description: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.

title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
description: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

title: Germany: Leipzig airport drone attack sets off alarm bells
description: German authorities have begun a counterterrorism ⁠investigation into a drone laden with explosives found near a Ukrainian transport plane at Leipzig Airport. It is seen as a "hybrid attack scenario."

title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football
description: Gianni Infantino is staying on as FIFA president despite growing pressure to step down. So who is football's most powerful man, why did UEFA and others turn against him, and how did he reassert his authority?

title: Germany: 10 years of 'Integration Act' for refugees
description: The German Integration Act aimed to regulate the integration of recognized refugees following high levels of immigration, facilitating access to the labor market in return for integration efforts.

title: Early settlement dynamics in the Pacific revealed through ancient DNA

title: Stable RNA elements open new possibilities for mRNA therapeutics
description: A research team led by Director Kim V. Narry at the Center for RNA Research within the Institute for Basic Science (IBS) has discovered compact viral RNA elements that can make mRNA more stable and increase protein production. These elements could provide a simple way to develop longer-lasting and more efficient mRNA technologies for vaccines and other RNA-based therapeutics.

title: A stress hormone may help the brain repair itself
description: A surprising stress-related signal may help the brain repair itself after injury. Researchers found that myelin-producing precursor cells rapidly release the stress hormone CRH near damaged brain tissue, helping control how those cells mature and rebuild protective nerve insulation. The same system also influences brain development and the thickness of myelin later in life. The findings could off…

title: World’s first superconducting quantum heat engine could help unlock massive quantum computers
description: A tiny superconducting engine has successfully converted heat near absolute zero into useful work, demonstrating the first cyclic quantum heat engine of its kind. Future versions could operate autonomously inside quantum computers, potentially eliminating huge numbers of costly, noise-producing microwave cables.

title: Scientists detect a nuclear reactor’s ghostly afterglow for the first time
description: Nuclear reactors may go dark, but their fuel continues producing a faint antineutrino “glow” long after shutdown. Researchers have now detected that residual signal for the first time, finding it closely matched predictions of radioactive decay inside the reactor and nearby spent-fuel pools. The breakthrough suggests antineutrino detectors could eventually monitor reactors even when they are offl…

title: Immune cells flood into the aging brain, Stanford scientists discover
description: Scientists have discovered that the aging human brain may be far less isolated from the rest of the body than once believed. Stanford researchers found that large numbers of immune cells from the blood begin entering the brain as early as middle age, where they can transform into microglia, the brain’s specialized immune cells. The finding overturns a long-standing assumption that these cells rem…

title: The Atlantic Ocean can handle more warming than expected — with one big catch
description: Scientists have found that the AMOC may be far more vulnerable to rapid warming than to temperature alone. When warming happens slowly, the ocean can adapt, but at faster rates similar to today’s, the massive Atlantic circulation could reach a tipping point at much lower temperatures.

title: Taking the stairs could protect your heart and help you live longer
description: Simply choosing the stairs could have surprisingly big benefits for your heart and longevity. A large analysis involving more than 480,000 people found that regular stair climbers were 39% less likely to die from cardiovascular disease and 24% less likely to die from any cause than people who rarely took the stairs. They also had lower risks of heart attack, stroke, and heart failure.

title: Women taking estrogen had fewer signs of Alzheimer’s in their brains
description: Women who used estrogen-only hormone therapy later in life were less likely to develop dementia and showed fewer signs of Alzheimer’s disease in their brains, according to a large study of more than 21,000 participants. Hormone therapy use was linked to 39% lower odds of a dementia diagnosis and 35% lower odds of Alzheimer’s-related brain changes at autopsy, including amyloid plaques and tau tang…

title: This common vitamin deficiency becomes far more dangerous when paired with belly fat
description: A large study of more than 5,500 adults over 50 found a striking combination of risk factors: abdominal obesity paired with vitamin D deficiency was linked to a 123% higher risk of death over six years. Each condition was associated with increased risk on its own, but together they appeared to create a dangerous feedback loop, with belly fat reducing the amount of vitamin D available in the blood…

title: Drinking orange juice every day may change thousands of genes
description: Orange juice may have a much bigger effect on the body than scientists once realized. Drinking it regularly appears to influence genes tied to inflammation, blood pressure, metabolism, and blood sugar control, while studies have also found improvements in cholesterol and blood vessel health. Researchers suspect natural citrus compounds such as hesperidin may be partly responsible. Even the gut mi…

title: Neptune’s tiny moons may be the wreckage of shattered ancient worlds
description: JWST has uncovered surprising clues that Neptune’s strange inner moons may be the wreckage of an ancient cosmic catastrophe. Researchers detected clay-like minerals on Larissa, Galatea, and Neptune’s rings that form in the presence of liquid water—yet the moons themselves show no obvious water ice. The material likely came from deep inside much larger icy moons that were shattered when Triton was…

title: A massive new cosmic map is revealing black holes, rare stars, and hidden gas
description: Astronomers have released more than three million new spectra in a sweeping expansion that, for the first time, brings SDSS-V optical observations to the Southern Hemisphere. The data reveal everything from rare stars and glowing nebulae to hundreds of thousands of X-ray sources and supermassive black holes changing over time.

title: JWST spots a bizarre “black hole star” 100 billion times brighter than a star
description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have discovered a bizarre object from just a few hundred million years after the Big Bang that looks like an enormous star but shines far too brightly to actually be one. The mysterious red object, dubbed a “black hole star,” may contain a black hole about 100,000 times the mass of the Sun wrapped inside a dense, star-like cocoon of hydrogen roughl…

title: A 236-million-year-old fossil could rewrite the story of mammalian birth
description: Scientists may have uncovered evidence that a mammal ancestor was giving birth to live young 236 million years ago. A fossilized cynodont showed a neonatal growth line and an unusually large birth size that closely match patterns seen in modern mammals. The discovery could push the evolution of live birth back by up to 95 million years. It also raises the possibility that many supposedly “modern”…

title: A surprising brain discovery could help explain why we overeat fatty foods
description: A protein inside appetite-controlling brain cells may play an important role in preventing overeating and obesity, particularly when high-fat foods are readily available. Unexpected differences between males and females could also help explain why obesity risk—and responses to weight-loss drugs—can vary.

title: Why your brain keeps making the same decisions – even when better options exist
description: Why do we keep making the same choices even when better options are available? Researchers found that simply repeating a decision can reshape what we prefer, causing familiar choices to feel better than alternatives. Instead of weighing every option from scratch, the brain often remembers what it chose before and repeats it. That shortcut may help explain many everyday habits and seemingly irrati…

title: Human brain cells are far more powerful than scientists thought
description: A single human brain cell may be far more powerful than scientists once realized. Researchers found that cortical neurons can perform remarkably complex computations, giving them capabilities more like tiny biological computers than simple on-off switches. This could help explain why the human brain supports abilities such as language, imagination, and mathematics.

title: One faulty gene copy can make the heart’s DNA fold the wrong way
description: Researchers have discovered that a gene linked to congenital heart disease acts like an architect for the heart cell’s DNA. Losing just one copy of TBX5 can cause the genome’s carefully folded 3D structure to unravel, disrupting the genes needed to build a healthy heart. The effects can vary from cell to cell, which may help explain why people with the same mutation develop different heart defect…

title: Scientists turn Starlink into a giant scanner for Earth’s upper atmosphere
description: Researchers have found a clever new way to map a part of Earth’s upper atmosphere that is notoriously difficult to observe. Using orbital data from roughly 1,200 Starlink satellites, they reconstructed changes in atmospheric density about 500 kilometers above Earth. The approach could sharpen satellite tracking and help reduce the growing risk of collisions in increasingly crowded orbits.

title: Scientists turn sheep’s wool into a material that helps regrow bone
description: Keratin extracted from sheep’s wool helped damaged bone regenerate in animals, producing tissue that was more organized and structurally similar to healthy bone than tissue grown with conventional collagen scaffolds. The discovery could turn an abundant agricultural byproduct into a promising new material for regenerative medicine.

title: James Webb captures a cosmic lion sculpted by a dying star
description: James Webb has captured a striking new infrared view of NGC 2392, the Lion Nebula, revealing the dramatic aftermath of a dying Sun-like star. At its center, a scorching white dwarf is blasting radiation into surrounding gas and dust, carving out the nebula’s lion-like face while illuminating a sprawling “mane” of surviving dusty clumps.

title: NASA’s Perseverance rover watches Earth vanish from the surface of Mars
description: NASA’s Perseverance rover caught a striking first from Mars: Earth disappearing behind the tiny moon Phobos. Seen from nearly 195 million miles away, our planet was reduced to a single point of light before briefly vanishing behind Phobos. The rare alignment created an unusual cosmic portrait of Earth as seen from another planet.

title: A surprising triple treatment completely clears hiv in newborn primates
description: Researchers have found a striking new way to potentially eliminate HIV soon after infection using a one-time combination of three therapies. In newborn nonhuman primates treated within three days of exposure, the regimen—standard antiretroviral drugs, broadly neutralizing antibodies, and the experimental antibody leronlimab—completely cleared the virus, even though none of the treatments could do…

title: The adult brain can repair itself better than scientists thought
description: The adult brain may be far better at repairing itself than scientists once believed. In mice, researchers discovered a special group of support cells called astrocytes that respond to damaged brain tissue by rebuilding lost cellular networks. Rather than simply moving into the injured area, these cells perform a remarkable maneuver: they create new nuclei and send them traveling through long cell…

title: A strange crystal made of electrons just revealed its hidden motion
description: Physicists have found a new way to peer inside one of matter’s most elusive quantum states: the Wigner crystal, where electrons stop behaving like independent particles and organize into a crystal-like pattern. By shining light on an atomically thin material cooled close to absolute zero, researchers uncovered optical signals that reveal not just where the electrons are, but how they move togethe…

title: Paleontology rocked by organic molecules found in 66-million-year-old dinosaur bones
description: Researchers have found strong evidence that original collagen can survive inside dinosaur fossils for tens of millions of years, overturning a long-standing assumption about fossilization. The discovery could unlock hidden molecular clues about dinosaur biology, evolution, and how ancient proteins managed to survive for so long.

title: Ordinary WiFi can now identify you with near-perfect accuracy
description: Ordinary WiFi networks could quietly become powerful surveillance tools, allowing people to be identified without cameras, special sensors, or even carrying a connected device. Researchers showed that unencrypted signals routinely exchanged between WiFi devices and routers can be used to create radio-based images of people and recognize them within seconds. In tests involving 197 participants, th…

title: “Cannot be explained” – New super steel stuns scientists
description: Scientists have created an unusually corrosion-resistant stainless steel that could replace costly titanium components used to produce green hydrogen. The breakthrough could reduce structural material costs by roughly 40 times and make seawater-based hydrogen production far more economical.

title: Scientists discover a hidden brain rhythm that could improve Parkinson’s treatment
description: Scientists have pinpointed a brain network—and its distinctive electrical rhythm—that appears to drive the benefits of deep brain stimulation for Parkinson’s disease. The discovery could lead to more precise, personalized stimulation settings and better results for patients.

title: Black holes older than the Big Bang could explain dark matter
description: Some black holes roaming the Universe today may actually be older than the Big Bang. A new cosmic “bounce” model suggests the Universe expanded from an earlier contracting phase, allowing ancient black holes to survive the transition as cosmic fossils. These relics could potentially explain dark matter and why surprisingly massive objects appeared so early in cosmic history.

title: 3,500-year-old skeletons challenge what scientists thought they knew about syphilis
description: Ancient remains from Vietnam suggest diseases like yaws may have been passed from mother to child thousands of years ago, a form of transmission often assumed to indicate syphilis. The discovery could overturn how scientists interpret ancient infections and complicate the long-running mystery of syphilis’s origins.

title: MIT neuroscientists discover the brain can reason without words
description: MIT neuroscientists have found striking evidence that language and logical reasoning are powered by separate systems in the brain. Even people with severe language impairments caused by stroke were able to solve challenging logic puzzles as well as people without those impairments, while brain scans showed that language-processing regions stayed largely quiet during reasoning tasks.

title: Ozempic may have revealed the brain’s hidden “craving center”
description: Ozempic-like drugs appear to weaken more than hunger—they may also reduce cravings for alcohol and other addictive substances. Scientists are increasingly tracing this effect to the lateral septum, a brain region that helps connect memories and surroundings with rewarding experiences. Packed with GLP-1 receptors, it may act as a crucial control point between thinking about a reward and feeling co…

title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
description: Scientists probing life’s deepest origins have uncovered evidence that the first free-living cells may have emerged not once, but twice. The findings suggest a striking possibility: life may share one ancient genetic code, yet have undergone two separate transitions into free-living existence.

title: Dogs can tell fear from sadness — and scientists saw it in their brains
description: Dogs may understand our emotions more deeply than scientists realized. Brain scans show that happy human faces activate regions in dogs linked to higher-level processing and reward, suggesting that smiles carry special emotional significance for them.

title: Scientists discover the brain has a fast lane and slow lane for clearing waste
description: AI has helped scientists measure the brain’s hidden cleaning system, revealing that fluid moves rapidly around its outer spaces but about 50 times more slowly through deep tissue. The discovery could eventually help researchers detect circulation problems linked to Alzheimer’s, aging, and concussions.

title: King Harold may have lost England by backing the wrong pope
description: A forgotten fragment of a lost papal letter is offering a surprising new explanation for the Norman Conquest. England may have backed the wrong pope during a bitter religious power struggle, giving Pope Alexander II a political reason to support William the Conqueror’s invasion. The discovery suggests Harold’s downfall in 1066 was shaped by intrigue in Rome as well as bloodshed at Hastings.

title: Marine heatwaves are harming human health in surprising ways
description: Marine heatwaves are emerging as a threat not just to coral reefs and fisheries, but to human health and well-being. Researchers warn that unusually hot oceans can fuel stronger storms, trigger harmful algal blooms, reduce seafood supplies, disrupt livelihoods, and contribute to anxiety, grief, and depression in coastal communities.

title: 150-million-year-old dinosaur footprints reveal something strange about its walk
description: A spectacular 150-million-year-old trail of more than 130 footprints captures a giant sauropod making a complete loop before continuing on its way. Its uneven stride hints that the long-necked dinosaur may have been walking with a limp.

title: A simple blood test could detect multiple cancers and reveal where they started
description: UCLA researchers have created a blood test that can scan DNA signals for multiple cancers, liver diseases, and signs of organ damage—and even indicate where trouble may be developing. Early results suggest the inexpensive approach could bring medicine closer to a single blood test capable of catching a wide range of diseases before they become harder to treat.

title: The secret hidden in these ancient manuscripts isn’t written in ink
description: Researchers can now recover DNA from centuries-old parchment without damaging the manuscripts, turning historic documents into unexpected genetic time capsules. The hidden clues could reveal ancient trade routes, livestock history, manuscript origins, and details of everyday life stretching back more than a thousand years.

title: Exercise may help the aging brain “take out the trash”
description: Regular exercise may help the brain clear away harmful waste that can build up with age. Researchers found that physical activity supports several processes linked to the brain’s glymphatic cleanup system, including better sleep, lower inflammation, and healthier blood vessels. Because this waste-removal system becomes increasingly important as we get older, exercise could play a meaningful role…

title: New GLP-1 pill delivers up to 12% weight loss in 36 weeks
description: An experimental GLP-1 pill helped people with obesity or overweight lose as much as 12.1% of their body weight in just 36 weeks. Unlike injectable drugs such as Wegovy and Ozempic, aleniglipron is a small molecule that can be taken once daily with or without food and could potentially be produced more easily at scale.

title: Scientists discover a hidden switch inside silver nanocatalysts
description: Silver nanocatalysts have been found to switch where they perform their most important reactions depending on whether a solid oxide cell is making electricity or hydrogen. The discovery could enable smarter catalyst designs that boost clean power generation while making green hydrogen more energy-efficient.

title: The sun will vanish over Europe in a rare total solar eclipse: Watch live
description: A total solar eclipse will plunge parts of Europe into darkness on August 12, 2026, with Spain offering some of the best views. ESA will livestream the spectacle from the Javalambre Observatory, combining telescope feeds, drone footage, and expert commentary. At 20:31 CEST, the observatory will experience 1 minute and 21 seconds of totality, revealing the Sun’s normally hidden outer atmosphere.

title: NASA’s moon base is taking shape with 20+ lunar landings planned

More than 20 landings are planned through 2029, testing everything from precision landings and lunar communications to rovers, power systems, and technology that can survive the Moon’s extreme conditions. Upcoming missions could also make history by exploring the Moon’s…

title: Voyager 2 was running out of power. NASA just bought it more time
description: NASA engineers have found a clever way to squeeze more life out of Voyager 2, nearly half a century after it left Earth. In an operation nicknamed the “Big Bang,” the team simultaneously shut down certain power-hungry hardware and switched to lower-power alternatives while keeping the spacecraft warm enough to survive.

title: For 15,000 years, humans and dogs have been changing each other
description: Dogs have been shaping—and being shaped by—humans for about 15,000 years, evolving from early partners of hunter-gatherers into an astonishing range of specialized companions. Across the globe, they adapted alongside people to wildly different environments and needs, from powerful Arctic sled dogs and agile rainforest hunters to high-altitude dogs with genetic traits for surviving thin air. Some…

title: 60,000-year-old ostrich eggshell engravings reveal a surprisingly sophisticated human mind
description: More than 60,000 years ago, humans in southern Africa were engraving ostrich eggshells with intricate geometric patterns that appear far more organized than previously realized. Researchers found recurring grids, parallel lines, right angles, and repeated shapes, suggesting the designs followed deliberate rules rather than being improvised. The engravers may even have planned entire patterns in t…

title: 1 in 5 people may carry this hidden genetic heart risk
description: Very high levels of the inherited cholesterol-related particle Lp(a) were linked to a greater risk of major cardiovascular events, particularly stroke and cardiovascular death, in a study of more than 20,000 people. Since elevated Lp(a) often flies completely under the radar, a simple blood test could uncover hidden heart risk that standard cholesterol testing may miss.

title: Wine, beer, or spirits? Massive study finds a surprising health divide
description: A study tracking more than 340,000 adults for over a decade found that heavy drinking increased the risk of death regardless of beverage type. At lower levels, however, the picture became more surprising: beer, cider, and spirits were linked to higher mortality, while wine was associated with lower risk. Moderate wine drinkers had a 21% lower risk of cardiovascular death compared with people who…

title: Potatoes may have given Indigenous Andeans a digestive superpower
description: The rise of the potato in the Andes appears to have left a lasting mark on human DNA. Indigenous Peruvians carry exceptionally high numbers of a starch-digestion gene, likely because people with more copies gained an evolutionary advantage once potatoes became a staple food. The change began thousands of years before European contact, providing unusually strong evidence that diet can shape human…

title: A daily glass of fruit juice was linked to lower depression scores
description: A daily glass of 100% fruit juice or a smoothie may help improve more than just fruit intake. In a small four-week trial, participants who added one to a healthier diet showed significantly lower depression scores, hinting that a simple dietary change could also support mental well-being.

title: Scientists find the strength training “sweet spot” for a longer life
description: Just a couple of hours of strength training each week could have surprisingly powerful effects on longevity. People who lifted weights for around 90 to 120 minutes weekly had a 13% lower risk of dying early, with especially large reductions in deaths from cardiovascular and neurological diseases. Pairing strength training with regular aerobic exercise was even more impressive, lowering overall de…

title: 240-million-year-old reptile fossil reveals a lost chapter before dinosaurs and crocodiles
description: A 240-million-year-old reptile discovered in Brazil is revealing what evolution looked like just before the rise of dinosaurs and crocodiles. The small predator had unusually positioned legs that may have allowed it to move more efficiently than many earlier reptiles. Its close relatives were previously known mostly from other continents, suggesting these ancient animals spread much farther acros…

title: Frequent cannabis users wake up with their “stress hormone” already elevated

Researchers say the finding raises questions about whether using cannabis for stress relief might, over time, interfere with the very system that helps the body handle stress.

title: For decades, we were told to choose low-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
description: Full-fat dairy may be healthier than conventional advice has suggested. description: An intensive seven-day meditation retreat triggered striking changes across the brain and body, including shifts tied to neuroplasticity, immunity, metabolism, and natural pain relief. description: Changing how much sweet-tasting food people eat may not change how much they crave or enjoy sweetness after all. description: Cassini data has revealed a surprising twist in Saturn’s magnetic shield: the planet’s rapid rotation appears to drag a key opening in its magnetosphere far toward the afternoon side instead of keeping it near noon, as happens on Earth. description: These four tiny glands in the neck — each roughly the size of a grain of rice — help regulate calcium levels in the body, which are essential for healthy bones, muscles, nerves, and kidneys.

description: A new 24-voice auditioned student ensemble devoted to the study and performance of Black sacred music will be led by renowned conductor Jeffrey Allen Murdock, who began his appointment at Yale on July 1.

title: Activists protest West Bank home sieges by Israeli occupiers

Israeli troops blocked access, declaring the area a closed military zone, though protesters managed to deliver essential supplies to the besieged families.

title: Europe steps up Ukraine aid but US arms remain vital
description: European donors have significantly increased military aid to Ukraine, driven largely by an €11 billion loan facility. However, a new report reveals that Europe remains heavily dependent on US weapons systems, with 30% of its defense procurement for Kyiv sourced from American companies.

title: Pakistan celebrates Independence Day with unity, peace calls
description: Pakistan marked its 79th Independence Day with nationwide rallies, flag-hoisting ceremonies, and special prayers. Leaders urged national unity, economic progress, and regional stability, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif highlighting the country's achievements and its defense partnership with Türkiye and Saudi Arabia.

title: Fidan: Egypt, Türkiye to deepen 'excellent' bilateral ties
description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan affirmed that Ankara and Cairo will continue strengthening their "excellent" relations based on mutual trust and shared interests. Speaking after co-chairing the Türkiye-Egypt Joint Planning Group meeting, he stressed that enhanced cooperation serves regional peace, stability, and prosperity.

title: Swiss farmers fear losses exceeding 2003 drought record
description: Markus Ritter of the Swiss Farmers' Union warned that drought losses could exceed the 500 million Swiss francs recorded in 2003, noting that exceptional heat and soil moisture deficits have created unprecedented conditions across the agricultural sector.

title: New Zealand Football withdraws support for Infantino reelection bid
description: New Zealand Football announced on Friday that it has formally withdrawn its support for Gianni Infantino's bid for a fourth term as FIFA president, citing a breakdown in trust over the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal and calling for an independent review to restore confidence in the governing body's decision-making processes.

title: China dismisses Taiwan war games as 'charade', waste of resources
description: China's Defense Ministry on Friday dismissed Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military exercises as a "charade" and waste of resources, as the island launched its largest war games since 1984 to test combat readiness amid rising tensions across the Taiwan Strait.

title: AK Party marks 25 years as Türkiye's dominant political force
description: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's Justice and Development (AK) Party celebrates 25 years since its 2001 founding, having governed Türkiye longer than any party since the multi-party era began in 1946 while steering the country through constitutional reforms and the transition to a presidential system.

title: Putin open to US envoys, but 'question is what they bring'
description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov confirmed President Vladimir Putin is ready to receive American envoys in Moscow, but stressed the substance of their proposals is what matters. The remarks come amid reports that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Russia and Ukraine to revive stalled peace efforts.

title: Türkiye hails Pakistan on Independence Day, vows unity
description: Türkiye's National Defense Ministry extended warm congratulations to Pakistan on its Independence Day, reaffirming the deep-rooted fraternal bonds between the two nations. Ankara pledged to stand alongside Islamabad in preserving their shared heritage and building a stronger future together.

title: Japan mulls response to Putin's disputed island visit
description: Tokyo is weighing potential measures against Moscow after President Vladimir Putin visited Iturup Island, part of a Russian-controlled chain claimed by Japan. A senior diplomat confirmed sanctions are under consideration, as bilateral tensions persist over the long-standing territorial dispute.

title: Panama Canal marks 112 years as global trade lifeline
description: The Panama Canal continues to underpin global maritime commerce on its 112th anniversary, connecting 180 shipping routes and 1,920 ports. The 77-kilometer waterway handled over 13,400 transits in 2025, generating $5.7 billion in revenue while remaining vital to US trade and Panama's economy.

title: Sudan floods displace nearly 1,000 families in North Darfur
description: Torrential rains and flash floods have displaced 975 families and damaged over 1,300 homes in North Darfur's Tawila locality. The disaster compounds the suffering of civilians already reeling from Sudan's ongoing conflict between the army and paramilitary forces.

title: Global markets buoyed by US inflation data, Mideast woes linger
description: Cooler-than-expected US inflation has pushed Fed rate hike expectations to December, weakening the dollar below 100. However, persistent Middle East uncertainty and high energy prices are capping investor optimism, with global equities trading mixed amid geopolitical tensions.

title: President Erdogan hails AK Party's 25-year 'historic transformation' of Türkiye
description: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan marks the Justice and Development Party's silver anniversary, highlighting sweeping advances in democracy, infrastructure, defense, and foreign policy. He pledges renewed focus on economic stability, technology, and institutional reforms for Türkiye's second century.

title: Tanker struck by drone in Strait of Hormuz: UK agency
description: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said Friday that a tanker sustained minor damage when struck by an uncrewed aerial vehicle during an outbound transit of the Strait of Hormuz, advising vessels to exercise caution amid heightened tensions in the strategic waterway.

title: US sailors face mental health crisis aboard aircraft carrier
description: US Navy personnel aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln are experiencing a severe psychological crisis after 250 consecutive days at sea during the Iran conflict. Reports indicate suicide attempts, deteriorating living conditions including moldy showers and broken toilets, while Washington shifts back to economic sanctions against Tehran.

title: Iran war drives US gas prices to $4, reshaping political landscape
description: The six-month US-Iran conflict has pushed national gasoline prices to the politically sensitive $4 per gallon threshold, with inflation data and voter surveys suggesting the economic burden is emerging as a major domestic liability for the Trump administration.

title: US backs Japan's claim to disputed islands after Putin visit
description: US Ambassador to Japan George Glass said Washington remains unwavering in its recognition of Japanese sovereignty over the Northern Territories, following Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to the disputed Iturup Island and Tokyo's subsequent strong protest to Moscow.

title: China rejects New Zealand 'at scale' espionage allegations
description: The Chinese Embassy in Wellington on Friday dismissed the New Zealand Security Intelligence Service report as "groundless" and part of a "new wave of attacks" orchestrated by foreign forces, warning that Wellington would bear responsibility for any consequences should it fail to work with Beijing.

title: Trump adviser Kushner to visit Israel for Gaza plan talks
description: Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump's senior adviser, and Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, plan to visit Israel next week to advance the US proposal for the enclave amid Israeli objections to parallel disarmament and withdrawal timelines, Axios reported.

title: Fidan meets Arab League chief during Egypt diplomatic visit
description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan held talks with Arab League Secretary-General Nabil Fahmy and Egypt's intelligence chief in El-Alamein. The two-day visit includes a presidential audience and discussions on trade, energy, and regional crises.

title: US puts lower oil prices ahead of Iran nuclear deterrence
description: Vice President JD Vance has declared that keeping fuel costs down for American consumers is the administration's primary objective, ranking above preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Oil prices have already dropped significantly from earlier peaks, he noted.

title: Colombia quake death toll surges to 281, hundreds missing
description: The devastating magnitude 7.4 earthquake that struck western Colombia on Monday has claimed 281 lives, with 379 still unaccounted for. Nearly 4,000 people have been injured as rescue teams race against time to find survivors amid the rubble.

title: Russia downs 51 drones near key oil port in Leningrad
description: Russian air defense forces intercepted 51 drones over the Leningrad region in an overnight attack targeting the Ust-Luga oil hub. Authorities reported a fire at the port following the barrage, though the drone threat has since been neutralized.

title: Albanese asks Trump to spare Australia from US tariffs
description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese personally appealed to President Donald Trump for a tariff exemption during a 40-minute phone call. Trump reportedly agreed to consider the request, as Canberra disputes Washington's justification linked to forced labor concerns.

title: Farage secures landslide Clacton by-election victory
description: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage swept back into Parliament with over 60% of the vote in a unique by-election he triggered himself. The contest featured a record 34 candidates, with major parties standing aside as Farage faced scrutiny over undisclosed financial gifts.

title: Saudi crown prince, US centcom chief hold talks on regional stability
description: Mohammed bin Salman and Admiral Brad Cooper convened to discuss defense cooperation and de-escalation efforts amid rising Gulf tensions. The meeting coincides with the formal activation of a 13-nation maritime alliance aimed at securing strategic waterways.

title: Besiktas edge Hradec Kralove to book Europa League playoff berth

title: Turkish-Egyptian relations at peak, Fidan says during visit

title: US Central Command launches multinational attack drone task force
description: The US Central Command announced the creation of Task Force Falcon Strike, a multinational unit integrating air, surface and underwater drone systems, as Washington seeks to deepen military cooperation with regional allies nine months after establishing its first dedicated attack drone squadron.

title: Syria and Russia discuss Latakia airport handover procedures

title: Lavrov accuses EU of 'robbery' and 'piracy' over cargo seizures

title: Palestine urges US, world to stop settler attacks in West Bank

title: Qarabag overturn first-leg deficit to reach Conference League playoffs

title: Erdogan hails 'historic step' as National Solidarity bill clears parliament

title: Russia ready to host US envoys Witkoff, Kushner once plans clear
description: Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said Thursday that Moscow stands ready to receive US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for talks once their visit itinerary becomes clear, while flatly denying that Washington has relayed any new Ukrainian peace proposals to the Kremlin through diplomatic channels.

title: PKK realizes it cannot achieve separatist goals: Erdogan

title: US deploying diplomatic, military tools to pressure Iran: Vance
description: US Vice President JD Vance said Washington is leveraging diplomatic, military and economic levers against Tehran to block its nuclear ambitions and secure energy flows, while cautioning that Iranian commitments remain unreliable.

title: US can sustain Iran blockade indefinitely, says Hegseth
